title: Equations of tangents and normals
keyIdea: The tangent at x = a has gradient f′(a) and passes through (a, f(a)). The normal is perpendicular to it.

kid: To find the tangent to a curve at a point, you need a gradient and a point. The derivative gives the gradient. The curve gives the point.
For y = x² at x = 3, the point is (3, 9). dy/dx = 2x, so the gradient is 6. Then 9 = 6 × 3 + c gives c = −9. So the tangent is y = 6x − 9.
adult: Use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), with m = f′(a) and the point (a, f(a)). Rearrange into y = mx + c if needed.
The normal is the line at right angles to the tangent at the same point. Its gradient is −1 ÷ m, because perpendicular gradients multiply to −1. For y = x² at (3, 9), the normal has gradient −1/6.

familyTip: Plot y = x² on graph paper. Draw your tangent at x = 3 and check that it just touches the curve.
